mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns; a lower rate compresses discount rates, increasing equity valuations and producing positive 20-day returns. This relationship is continuous and active without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This threshold is based on historical recession signals where unemployment exceeds 5.5%.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) captures the dual strength of manufacturing output and consumer housing demand. When both series are rising, it indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This interaction effect is stronger than the individual series effects and is always active as a continuous signal.
failure_condition: The interaction term (INDPRO * HOUST) shows Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the interaction effect is not significant in a multivariate regression (p>0.05) when controlling for other macro variables.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand for goods (RSAFS) exceeds 450,000, it signals strong consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is most powerful during late-cycle expansion when consumer spending is a leading indicator of economic strength.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances where RSAFS > 450000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is a leading indicator of inflation expectations; a monthly increase above 0.3% signals rising inflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This relationship is due to the market's immediate reaction to inflation data releases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in < 40% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 240 (index) signals accelerating inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This threshold is based on historical periods where inflation exceeded 240 (1982-1984=100) and equity markets underperformed.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between employment growth (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) captures the dual strength of labor market and manufacturing output. When both series are rising, it indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This interaction effect is stronger than the individual series effects and is always active as a continuous signal.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * INDPRO) shows Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the interaction effect is not significant in a multivariate regression (p>0.05) when controlling for other macro variables.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This relationship is due to the market's immediate reaction to strong labor market data.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
